speaker: provenzano
text: Thank you, Madam Clerk. I wanna welcome everybody to our last meeting of 2021. I wanna thank our broadcasting partners and our media partners for broadcasting our media and reporting on it. Before we start the meeting, I just want to speak to the community briefly about the current state of COVID-19 in our community. You know, in the last number of weeks, we've gone from having a very low prevalence of COVID-19 to a very high prevalence of COVID-19. And I understand that all of us, myself included, are frustrated by the length of this and finding it difficult to make the sacrifices that we need to make to combine with COVID-19 health guidance. So I wanna just ask the community as we head into the Christmas season, if we can all dig deep and keep a few things really top of mind. It's important that all of us reduce our contacts as much as we can. That's not to say that we can't see some friends and family, but we should really make sure that when we do so, we do so safely and that when we do so, it's more of an important event as opposed to just a discretionary event. So we wanna reduce our COVID-19 contacts as much as possible. When you are inside, we encourage you to make sure you are wearing a mask and that you're staying physically distant from people. It's best to interact with people and socialize with people in a well-ventilated area, preferably outside if the weather permits. And we wanna make sure that we are all doing whatever we can to help slow the spread of the virus. It's pretty clear based on the data and the evidence that's been shared to date and been assessed by people that are a lot smarter than I am that the new variant of COVID-19 is very transmissible and its case counts seem to double every three days. So at that rate, we could have a very significant case count, not just in the province of Ontario, but in our own community of Sault Ste. Marie that could put stress on our medical system. So I wanna encourage all of you that have not been vaccinated to consider getting vaccinated, get information from reliable sources, speak to your healthcare providers. If you have children that can be vaccinated, I encourage you to get your children vaccinated. If you have your first and second dose and you qualify for your third dose, I encourage you to get your third dose. If you have your first dose and you can get your second dose, I encourage you to get your second dose. Reduce your contacts as much as you can. Wear a mask when you're inside. Engage with people as best as you can outside. Make sure that when you are inside, you're in properly ventilated spaces and you are staying physically distant. I have a lot of confidence in our community and the fact that we can end the year strong and begin the next year strong. And I'd encourage all of you to be mindful of the advice that public health is sharing with us and to follow that advice. So I'd encourage before we start our meeting, I wanna acknowledge the territory upon which we are gathered, subject to the Huron Robinson Treaty, traditional territory of Anishinaabe, specifically Garden River First Nation, Batchewana First Nation, and the Historic Sault Ste. Marie-Médie Council. I wanna recognize that we are the home, the head office of Missinati-Cree First Nation. I wanna recognize the Indigenous Friendship Center and their partnership with our community. I wanna thank all of them for sharing their territory with us, historically known as Bawotay. Madam Clerk, if you can start the meeting, please.

speaker: donnahilsinger
